ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a transition-state structure, with the main body being a six-membered ring; the top of the ring is connected to a carbonyl C=O, the ring carbon on the right is connected to OH, and below the ring is connected to a side-chain carbon; this side-chain carbon is further connected separately to R and NH. Curved arrows and hydrogen-related labels such as H and H+ are also drawn in the figure. Then reason: Ignore arrows as required and exclude bonds involving hydrogen. The connections of the six heavy atoms of the six-membered ring count as 6; the top carbonyl C=O counts as 1; the connection from the right ring carbon to the oxygen in OH counts as 1; the connection from the lower ring carbon to the side-chain carbon counts as 1; the connection from the side-chain carbon to R counts as 1; the connection from the side-chain carbon to the nitrogen in NH counts as 1. The total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. Disregard arrows and consider all components present in the transition-state structure.

method.method_draft: Scan the image component by component. Count the six heavy-atom connections making the six-membered ring as 6. Add the carbonyl C=O connection at the top as 1. Add the ring-to-OH connection on the right as 1. Add the lower ring carbon-to-side-chain carbon connection as 1. Add the side-chain carbon-to-R connection as 1. Add the side-chain carbon-to-NH connection as 1, while excluding the N-H and O-H/H labels. Total these non-hydrogen connections: 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11.

method.method_draft: Assign heavy-atom degrees from the image: carbonyl O degree 1; carbonyl ring carbon degree 3; top-right ring carbon degree 2; right ring carbon bearing OH degree 3; OH oxygen degree 1; lower ring carbon attached to the side chain degree 3; lower-left ring carbon degree 2; upper-left ring carbon degree 2; side-chain carbon attached to R and NH degree 3; R group degree 1; NH nitrogen degree 1. planner_metadata.image_role: From the image, map each non-hydrogen atom/group as a graph node: the six ring atoms, the top carbonyl oxygen, the right OH oxygen, the lower side-chain carbon, the R group, and the imine NH nitrogen. Record only visible heavy-atom adjacencies; ignore curved arrows and explicit hydrogens.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the problem text to decide that hydrogen bonds are omitted, arrows are not graph edges, and every displayed structural component, including R and NH, must be included.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In an undirected connectivity graph, each bond contributes 2 to the total degree count, so the number of bonds is half the sum of heavy-atom degrees. Double bonds are still one adjacency/bond connection for this count.
